record.paper_title: Research Problems on Relations Between Nijenhuis Geometry and Integrable Systems
record.context_brief: Unity conditions in induced algebra structures
record.original_question: For the algebra structure produced from a differentially non-degenerate Nijenhuis operator and a symmetry M, which differential conditions are satisfied by the unity field, given that the construction already satisfies almost all of the F-manifold axioms except the differential conditions on the unity?

evidence.quote: (5) We have constructed an algebra structure which satisfies almost all conditions, except for differential conditions on the unity. Which conditions does the unity satisfy in our case, for example, for a differentially non-degenerate Nijenhuis operator?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a smooth manifold of dimension $n$ equipped with a $(1,1)$-tensor field $L$ whose Nijenhuis torsion
$$
\mathcal{N}_L(X,Y)\;=\;L^2[X,Y]-L[LX,Y]-L[X,LY]+[LX,LY]
$$
vanishes identically; such an $L$ is called a Nijenhuis operator. Assume $L$ is differentially non-degenerate at every point, meaning that the differentials $d(\operatorname{tr} L),\, d(\operatorname{tr} L^2),\,\ldots,\, d(\operatorname{tr} L^n)$ are pointwise linearly independent. Let $M$ be a symmetry of $L$, i.e. another $(1,1)$-tensor field commuting with $L$ in the sense that $[L,M]=0$ and whose Nijenhuis-type compatibility with $L$ holds, and suppose that the construction $(L,M)\mapsto (\circ,e)$ produces on $TM$ a fibrewise commutative associative multiplication $\circ$ with a distinguished vector field $e$ playing the role of a unity (i.e. $e\circ X=X$ for all $X$).

Recall that an F-manifold structure on $M$ consists of such a commutative associative multiplication $\circ$ on $TM$ with unity $e$, satisfying the Hertling–Manin condition
$$
\mathcal{L}_{X\circ Y}(\circ)\;=\;X\circ \mathcal{L}_Y(\circ)+Y\circ \mathcal{L}_X(\circ),
$$
together with the differential conditions on the unity
$$
\mathcal{L}_e(\circ)=0\qquad\text{and}\qquad \mathcal{L}_e(e)=0.
$$

Assume that the algebra structure $(\circ,e)$ produced from the differentially non-degenerate Nijenhuis operator $L$ and its symmetry $M$ satisfies every F-manifold axiom except possibly the differential conditions on the unity $e$. Determine explicitly which differential identities the unity vector field $e$ satisfies in this construction; in particular, decide whether $\mathcal{L}_e(\circ)=0$ and $\mathcal{L}_e(e)=0$ hold, and if not, describe the precise residual identities involving $\mathcal{L}_e(\circ)$, $\mathcal{L}_e(e)$, $L$, and $M$.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as a research problem in a 2024 collection on Nijenhuis geometry and integrable systems. Related work by Antonov and others (e.g., "Nijenhuis operators with a unity and F-manifolds", JLMS 2024; "Almost differentially nondegenerate Nijenhuis operators", 2025) establishes the link between Nijenhuis operators with cyclic unity and regular F-manifolds, but does not provide a complete answer to which differential conditions the induced unity satisfies in the symmetry-based construction. No source found that resolves the specific question, so it appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Nijenhuis operators with a unity and F-manifolds
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes that regular F-manifolds coincide with Nijenhuis manifolds with a cyclic unity, but does not address the symmetry construction in question.
status_evidence.claim: Closely related results on the unity / F-manifold link exist but do not resolve the differential conditions on the unity in the symmetry-induced algebra.

status_evidence.title: Almost Differentially Nondegenerate Nijenhuis Operators
status_evidence.snippet: Recent (2025) work continues to study differentially non-degenerate Nijenhuis operators, indicating the surrounding theory is actively developing.
status_evidence.claim: The differentially non-degenerate case remains an active research topic with open problems.

status_evidence.title: Research problems on relations between Nijenhuis geometry and integrable systems
status_evidence.snippet: Lists the question about which differential conditions the unity satisfies as an open research problem.
status_evidence.claim: The question is explicitly framed as an open problem.
